page: Microsoft Azure F1alds_v7 is a single-core virtual machine belonging to the Faldsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core, paired with a low-memory allocation of 2.0 GB RAM. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 118 GB, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded or memory-bound performance. The high-frequency AMD processor delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core tests and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks. However, due to the single-core limitation, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the weak category. Memory performance is also constrained, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10% and cached small-block read bandwidth rated as weak, though uncached large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average speeds.

The F1alds_v7 offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring high clock-speed execution without massive memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low resource density, specifically the 2.0 GB RAM limit and single-thread execution, which makes it poor for static web serving or database operations. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic utility scripting, or small-scale language model inference using small models, where high single-core frequency is advantageous but memory requirements are minimal.
